google_workspace.name: Google Workspace
google_workspace.dkim_switch: in the Admin console under Authenticate email, the Start authentication button

steps: Sign in to the Google Admin console as a super administrator.
Go to Menu > Apps > Google Workspace > Gmail, then click Authenticate email.
In the Selected domain menu, choose {domain}.
Click Generate New Record. Pick key length 2048 (pick 1024 only if your DNS provider cannot take 2048) and leave the prefix selector as google.
Click Generate, then copy the TXT record value Google shows. The record name is google._domainkey.{domain}.
At the company that hosts your DNS, add a TXT record with that name and that value. Do not click Start authentication yet.
When the record is live, go back to Authenticate email and click Start authentication. Google says a new Gmail setup can take 24 to 72 hours before the key is available.

microsoft_365.name: Microsoft 365
microsoft_365.dkim_switch: in the Defender portal, the Sign messages for this domain with DKIM signatures switch

steps: Sign in to the Microsoft Defender portal at security.microsoft.com.
Go to Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Email authentication settings, then open the DKIM tab.

Click the row for {domain} (not the on/off switch) to open its details panel. If it shows no CNAME values yet, slide the switch to Enabled once: an error box appears that holds the values. Click OK, then open the row again.
Under Publish CNAMEs you will see two values. Click Copy.
At the company that hosts your DNS, create two CNAME records: name selector1._domainkey.{domain} pointing to the first value, and name selector2._domainkey.{domain} pointing to the second value.
Wait a few minutes (it can take longer), reopen the details panel, and turn on Sign messages for this domain with DKIM signatures.

zoho.name: Zoho Mail
zoho.dkim_switch: in Zoho Mail Admin Console, the DKIM tab, where DKIM is enabled after the selector is verified

steps: Sign in to the Zoho Mail Admin Console as an administrator.
Open Domains in the left menu and select {domain}.
On the Email Configuration tab, select DKIM.
Add a new selector and name it zoho. Choose key length 2048 (or 1024 if your DNS provider cannot take 2048).
Copy the TXT value Zoho generates.
At the company that hosts your DNS, add a TXT record named zoho._domainkey.{domain} with that value. Some DNS providers add the domain for you; then type only zoho._domainkey.
Back in Zoho, click Verify next to the selector. When asked, enable DKIM so outgoing mail is signed.
In Mailchimp click your profile icon and choose Account & billing (account managers click Account).
Open the Domains tab and click Start authentication next to {domain}.
Choose your DNS provider in the drop-down and click Next.
Click Or manually authenticate your domain, choose your provider (or Other) and click Next.
At the company that hosts your DNS, add the two CNAME records (Name and Value) that Mailchimp shows. Then click Next in Mailchimp.
Mailchimp then asks for a DMARC record. Do not add a second one: a domain may have only one DMARC record, so use the DMARC line in this result.
Wait for Mailchimp to validate the records. It usually takes minutes but can take up to 48 hours.
In SendGrid go to Settings > Sender Authentication and click Get Started in the Domain Authentication section.
Choose your DNS host and choose whether to turn on link branding.
Enter {domain} as the root domain (no subdomain, no https://).
Open Advanced Settings and leave Use automated security ticked. With it on, SendGrid handles SPF through its CNAME records, so no extra SPF entry is needed.
Click Next to reach Install DNS Records and choose Manual Setup.

At the company that hosts your DNS, add the CNAME records SendGrid lists (one starting with em, plus s1._domainkey and s2._domainkey). If your DNS provider adds the domain for you, type only the part before it.
Click Verify in SendGrid. It can take up to 48 hours.
In the Mailgun control panel open {domain} and go to the Domain Verification & DNS section.
Copy the DKIM record shown there (its name and value are specific to your Mailgun account).
At the company that hosts your DNS, add that record exactly as shown.
Wait. Mailgun says this can take 24 to 48 hours.
Click Verify DNS settings in the Domain Settings section, or let Mailgun's automatic check pick it up.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the Amazon SES console.
In the left menu, under Configuration, choose Verified identities, then choose {domain}.
On the Authentication tab, expand View DNS records.
Copy the three Easy DKIM CNAME records. Each name ends in ._domainkey.{domain}.
At the company that hosts your DNS, add all three CNAME records exactly as shown. SPF needs no change unless you use a custom MAIL FROM domain.
